_comment: Roster metadata for the major outlets absent on 2026-09-22, keyed by the name in scripts/roster/majors_target.py. WHAT IS AND IS NOT A MEASUREMENT: name, url, country, tier and type are facts about the outlet. `political_lean_baseline` is NOT measured; it is the intended side from majors_target.py mapped conservatively (L -> center-left, C -> center, R -> center-right) so a new row is never claimed to be extreme on evidence nobody has. Every row's notes say so. The outlet-baseline programme measures them; until it does, a provisional inner placement keeps the outlet in the lean aggregate, which `unrated` would not, and understates rather than overstates.

The Mirror.notes: British tabloid, founded 1903. Labour-leaning. Trinity Mirror/Reach plc.

Irish Independent.notes: Ireland's largest-circulation daily, founded 1905. Mediahuis Ireland.

The Journal.ie.notes: Irish digital-native daily, founded 2010. Runs FactCheck, an IFCN signatory.

Liberation.notes: French daily, founded 1973 by Jean-Paul Sartre and Serge July.

Mediapart.notes: Subscriber-funded French investigative site, founded 2008. Broke the Cahuzac and Benalla affairs. Takes no advertising.

RFI.notes: Radio France Internationale, France's state-funded international broadcaster, editorially independent under France Medias Monde.

Le Figaro.notes: France's oldest national daily, founded 1826. Conservative. Dassault-owned.

Sueddeutsche Zeitung.notes: Munich daily, founded 1945. One of Germany's two largest national broadsheets. Panama Papers partner.

Die Zeit.notes: German weekly, founded 1946. Long-form and debate format.

taz.notes: Berlin daily, founded 1978, cooperatively owned by its readers.

Frankfurter Allgemeine.notes: German national daily of record, founded 1949. Owned by a nonprofit foundation.

Focus.notes: German weekly news magazine, founded 1993. Hubert Burda Media.

Il Fatto Quotidiano.notes: Italian daily, founded 2009. Takes no state subsidy.

Il Foglio.notes: Italian daily, founded 1996 by Giuliano Ferrara.

eldiario.es.notes: Spanish digital daily, founded 2012, majority-owned by its journalists. Member-funded.

Publico.notes: Spanish digital daily, founded 2007 as a print paper, online-only since 2012.

El Mundo.notes: Spanish national daily, founded 1989. Unidad Editorial.

ABC.notes: Spanish national daily, founded 1903. Monarchist and conservative. Vocento.

La Razon.notes: Spanish national daily, founded 1998. Planeta group.

La Vanguardia.notes: Barcelona daily, founded 1881. Catalonia's largest by circulation.

De Volkskrant.notes: Dutch national daily, founded 1919. DPG Media.

NRC.notes: Dutch national daily (NRC Handelsblad), founded 1970. Mediahuis.

Trouw.notes: Dutch national daily, founded 1943 as a resistance paper. DPG Media.

Elsevier Weekblad.notes: Dutch weekly news magazine, founded 1945, renamed EW Magazine in 2018.

Le Soir.notes: Francophone Belgian daily, founded 1887. Rossel group.

La Libre Belgique.notes: Francophone Belgian daily, founded 1884. IPM group.

Dagens Nyheter.notes: Sweden's largest morning daily, founded 1864. Bonnier.

Aftonbladet.notes: Sweden's largest news site, founded 1830. Part-owned by the trade union confederation LO.

Jyllands-Posten.notes: Danish national daily, founded 1871. JP/Politikens Hus.

Gazeta Wyborcza.notes: Polish daily, founded 1989 out of the Solidarity round-table talks. Agora.

Rzeczpospolita.notes: Polish daily of record on law and business, founded 1920.

Telex.notes: Hungarian digital daily, founded 2020 by the staff who resigned from Index. Reader-funded.

Denik N.notes: Czech subscriber-funded daily, founded 2018 by former Denik Referendum and Respekt journalists.

Publico (Portugal).notes: Portuguese national daily, founded 1990. Sonae group.

Die Presse.notes: Austrian daily, founded 1848. Styria Media Group.

Novaya Gazeta Europe.notes: Founded 2022 in Riga by Novaya Gazeta journalists after the Russian edition suspended publication. Six of its Russian predecessor's journalists have been murdered.

Meduza.notes: Russian-language outlet based in Riga, founded 2014 by the sacked Lenta.ru editorial team. Designated undesirable by Russia in 2023.

Duvar English.notes: English service of Gazete Duvar, founded 2019. Independent of the Turkish state media pool.

Asahi Shimbun.notes: Japanese national daily, founded 1879. Second-largest circulation in Japan.

Hankyoreh.notes: South Korean daily, founded 1988 by journalists dismissed under the military government, funded by a public share issue.

The Daily Star (Lebanon).notes: Lebanese English-language daily, founded 1952. Publication has been intermittent since 2020.

BusinessDay (SA).notes: South African business daily, founded 1985. Arena Holdings. Also syndicated on businesslive.co.za; the roster uses businessday.co.za, which is where its feed's articles live.

Ahram Online.notes: English service of Al-Ahram, an Egyptian state-owned daily founded 1875.

Mada Masr.notes: Egyptian independent outlet, founded 2013. Blocked inside Egypt since 2017.

O Globo.notes: Rio de Janeiro daily, founded 1925. Grupo Globo.

Clarin.notes: Argentina's largest-circulation daily, founded 1945. Grupo Clarin.

Reforma.notes: Mexico City daily, founded 1993. Grupo Reforma.

El Comercio.notes: Peru's oldest daily, founded 1839. Grupo El Comercio.

Stuff.notes: New Zealand's largest news site, founded 2000. Employee-owned since 2020.

_feed_tokens_comment: `feed_tokens` on an outlet lists extra strings its own feed title may use in place of its name: an abbreviation it puts in its masthead, or a name it has since taken. add_sources.py accepts a title matching one. Declared per outlet rather than by loosening the check, so a wrong equivalence is visible in this file.
